title: Changes in energy

concepts.def: The energy stored in an object because it is moving. It is calculated from kinetic energy = 0.5 x mass x (speed)^2, that is E_k = 1/2 m v^2, and it is zero when the object is at rest.

In E_k = 1/2 m v^2 the speed alone is squared, not the mass and not the product of the two. Doubling the speed of an object multiplies its kinetic energy by four, while doubling its mass only doubles the kinetic energy.

concepts.term: Units in the kinetic energy equation
concepts.def: Kinetic energy Ek is in joules, J; mass m is in kilograms, kg; speed v is in metres per second, m/s. A mass in grams or a speed in km/h must be converted first, or the answer will not be in joules.

The unit of every energy store in this section: kinetic, elastic potential and gravitational potential energy are all measured in joules. The newton is a unit of force and the watt is a unit of power, so neither can be the unit of an energy calculation.

The energy stored in a spring, or other elastic object, because it has been stretched or compressed. For a spring it is calculated from elastic potential energy = 0.5 x spring constant x (extension)^2, that is E_e = 1/2 k e^2.
A measure of how stiff a spring is: the force needed for each metre of extension. It is measured in newtons per metre, N/m, so a spring of large k needs a large force to stretch it a given amount.

The increase in the length of the spring, measured in metres, m. It is the stretched length minus the original unstretched length, not the stretched length itself, and it must be converted from centimetres or millimetres before it is squared.

The point beyond which extension is no longer proportional to the force applied. The equation E_e = 1/2 k e^2 is used only while the limit of proportionality has not been exceeded; past that point it no longer gives the energy stored.

The energy stored in an object because of its position in a gravitational field. The amount gained when an object is raised is calculated from g.p.e. = mass x gravitational field strength x height, that is E_p = m g h.
The force acting on each kilogram of mass, measured in newtons per kilogram, N/kg. Its value is always supplied in the question in this specification, so it never has to be recalled.

The vertical distance the object is raised above ground level, measured in metres, m. When an object is moved along a slope or a ramp, it is the vertical rise that is used as h, not the longer distance travelled along the surface.
In E_p = m g h the gravitational potential energy Ep is in joules, J; mass m is in kilograms, kg; gravitational field strength g is in newtons per kilogram, N/kg; and height h is in metres, m.

concepts.term: Units in the elastic potential energy equation
concepts.def: In E_e = 1/2 k e^2 the elastic potential energy Ee is in joules, J; the spring constant k is in newtons per metre, N/m; and the extension e is in metres, m.

Mass is the quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms, kg, and it is m in E_k = 1/2 m v^2 and E_p = m g h. No mass appears in E_e = 1/2 k e^2. Weight is a force in newtons and is never substituted for the mass.

Use E_k = 1/2 m v^2 when an object is moving, E_e = 1/2 k e^2 when a spring has been stretched, and E_p = m g h when an object has been raised. Only the kinetic and elastic equations contain a factor of 0.5.

mcqs.q: A ball of mass 500 g is moving at a speed of 6 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
options: 9 J

mcqs.q: A toy car of mass 0.8 kg is moving at a speed of 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
options: 2 J

mcqs.q: A van doubles its speed. Its mass does not change. What happens to its kinetic energy?
options: it becomes eight times as big as before
it becomes four times as large as before
it becomes twice as large as before
it stays the same size as before
mcqs.explain: Speed is squared in E_k = 1/2 m v^2, so a factor of 2 on the speed gives a factor of 2^2 = 4 on the energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the equation E_k = 1/2 m v^2 written out in words?
options: kinetic energy = 0.5 × (mass)^2 × (speed)
kinetic energy = 0.5 × mass × speed
kinetic energy = mass × (speed)^2
kinetic energy = 0.5 × mass × (speed)^2
mcqs.explain: This is the equation as the specification states it: the speed, and only the speed, is squared.

mcqs.q: A kinetic energy calculation uses a mass in kilograms and a speed in metres per second. The answer is in which unit?
options: newtons, N
watts, W
joules, J
kg m/s
mcqs.explain: Kinetic energy, like every energy store in this section, is measured in joules, J.

mcqs.q: A student puts the mass of a 250 g ball straight into E_k = 1/2 m v^2 as 250. Why is the answer wrong?
options: the speed should have been squared before the mass
the mass has to be in newtons, so m should be 2.5
the answer is right, but the unit is newtons
the mass has to be in kilograms, so m should be 0.25
mcqs.explain: The equation needs the mass in kilograms, and 250 g = 250/1000 = 0.25 kg.

mcqs.q: A car's speed is given as 72 km/h. What must be done before using E_k = 1/2 m v^2?
options: convert the speed to metres per second
convert the speed into kilometres per minute
use 72 as the speed and convert the answer
square 72 first and then halve the answer
mcqs.explain: The equation requires the speed v in m/s, so 72 km/h must be converted to 20 m/s first.

mcqs.q: Which pair of quantities is needed to calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object?
options: the force applied and the speed reached
the weight and the speed of the object
the mass and the speed of the object
the mass and the distance travelled
mcqs.explain: E_k = 1/2 m v^2 contains only the mass and the speed; nothing else about the object is needed.

mcqs.q: A spring has a spring constant of 200 N/m. It is stretched, within its limit of proportionality, so that its extension is 0.1 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored in the spring?
options: 1 J

mcqs.q: A spring with a spring constant of 400 N/m is stretched by an extension of 5 cm, staying within its limit of proportionality. How much elastic potential energy is stored?
options: 1 J

mcqs.q: The energy stored in a stretched spring is E_e = 1/2 k e^2. What do the symbols k and e stand for?
options: the spring constant and the energy of the spring
the spring constant and the force applied to it
the spring constant and the stretched length
the spring constant and the extension of the spring
mcqs.explain: k is the spring constant, in N/m, and e is the extension, in m.

mcqs.q: A spring is stretched within its limit of proportionality. The elastic potential energy stored in it is measured in which unit?
options: newtons, N
joules, J
watts, W
N/m
mcqs.explain: Elastic potential energy, like every energy store, is measured in joules, J.

mcqs.q: In the equation E_e = 1/2 k e^2, the spring constant k is measured in which unit?
options: newtons times metres, N m
newtons per kilogram, N/kg
newtons per centimetre, N/cm
newtons per metre, N/m
mcqs.explain: The spring constant is the force needed for each metre of extension, so it is measured in N/m.

mcqs.q: A spring of unstretched length 0.20 m is stretched to a length of 0.26 m. Which length is the extension e used in E_e = 1/2 k e^2?
options: the whole stretched length, in metres
the increase in length, in metres
the length before stretching, in metres
the extra length, in centimetres
mcqs.explain: The extension is 0.26 - 0.20 = 0.06 m, and the equation needs it in metres.

mcqs.q: A spring is stretched so far that its limit of proportionality has been exceeded. What does this mean for E_e = 1/2 k e^2?
options: the equation still works if e is measured again
the spring constant doubles from that point on
the equation can no longer be used to find the energy
the energy stored becomes zero at that point
mcqs.explain: The specification states the equation assuming the limit of proportionality has not been exceeded, so beyond that limit it does not apply.

mcqs.q: Which two quantities must be known to calculate the elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring?
options: the spring constant and the extension
the spring constant and the force used
the mass of the spring and its extension
the spring constant and the length
mcqs.explain: E_e = 1/2 k e^2 needs only the spring constant k, in N/m, and the extension e, in m.

mcqs.q: A book of mass 800 g is lifted through a height of 1.5 m. The gravitational field strength is 10 N/kg. How much gravitational potential energy does the book gain?
options: 6 J

mcqs.q: A box is pushed 5.0 m up a ramp and ends up 2.0 m above the ground. Which value is used as h in E_p = m g h?
options: 5.0 m, the distance moved along the ramp surface
3.0 m, the difference in the two distances
2.0 m, the vertical height risen above the ground
7.0 m, the two distances added together
mcqs.explain: h is the vertical height gained, and the path taken up the ramp does not change it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is g.p.e. = mass x gravitational field strength x height written in symbols, with the correct unit?
options: E_p = 1/2 m g h, giving E_p in joules
E_p = m g h, giving E_p in joules
E_p = m g h, giving E_p in watts
E_p = m g, giving E_p in joules
mcqs.explain: This is the equation as the specification states it, and Ep is measured in joules, J.

mcqs.q: In E_p = m g h, what is g and where does its value come from?
options: field strength in N/kg, which must be recalled
field strength in N, given in the exam question
the force of gravity in N, given in the question
field strength in N/kg, given in the question
mcqs.explain: Gravitational field strength is measured in newtons per kilogram, and the specification states that its value will be given.
